claim: R4-03 made an element a restoring event's re-cut mints enter the damage only when that restoration ends: "Before that week it is drawn as built" (V06 §3.23 (3)). V03 §5.6 (2) (a) (l. 2693–2694: "an element is compared with the level only from its entry week") and §2.6 step 7 (l. 2099–2101) carry it. R4-03's sweep cleared §8.6 and V02 l. 3058 for the `decayPeak` they read. Their restatements of the *damaged* comparison still omit the entry week. §8.6's lead (l. 14069–14072) has "each plan element whose threshold t … its decay level reaches at the drawn week (… damaged while the level is above 0 and at least t — §6.3 *Plan damage*'s one comparison every reader makes) is drawn damaged". V02 §5.7 (2) (l. 3057–3063) has "damaged, by §6.3 *Plan damage*'s one comparison (the level above 0 and at least its keyed threshold t …)", and it names only "a wing an `extend` adds, an element a re-cut makes … added after its building's damage left" as drawn as built. During a `reoccupy` whose `repair` Works still runs, a minted room's roof bay or partition whose t the level reaches is damaged by these two texts and as built by V03, V06 and §2.6. Both texts take each element's state from V03's `planDamage` (V03 §5.6 (3); V02 §5.7 (2): "V03's damage layer gives each element its state"), so nothing built changes. This is VDC4-01's case (§6.3, the home) at two restatements.
required_change: One fix with VDC4-01. §8.6's lead: after "(V06's `decayLevel`; damaged while the level is above 0 and at least t" insert ", compared from the element's entry week into the plan (V03 §5.6 (2) (a)–(b); an element a restoring event's re-cut mints from the week that restoration ends, before which it draws as built, V06 §3.23 (3))". END at V02 §5.7 (2): "damaged, by §6.3 *Plan damage*'s one comparison (the level above 0 and at least its keyed threshold t: §6.3's `plan.damage`, V11's ranges)" adds "from the element's entry week into the plan (V03 §5.6 (2) (a))", and "so an element added after its building's damage left (a wing an `extend` adds, an element a re-cut makes) is drawn as built" → "so an element added after its building's damage left (a wing an `extend` adds, an element a re-cut makes), or one a restoring event's re-cut mints (V06 §3.23 (3)), is drawn as built".

claim: Missed subject: the view-bound why for section providers. The why card's `plan` damage rows are read at the view's drawn week. V03 §5.6 (2) (d) (l. 2718–2721) says `own` serves 'the `plan` section's rows (V03 §4.6) … The week is the drawn week of the view or the export (§2.9's `week`; a scrubbed frame's, V06 §3.15.2), so scrubbing history shows one plan aging'. V09 §2.12's damage-lines row (l. 1010) derives them 'at V06's `decayLevel` for the drawn week' for 'the plan panel; the why card's `plan` section'. V09 §4.21.13 (1) and V10 §3.9a's `info.damage.head.<state>` row (l. 1838) give 'the whole years of its decay run at the drawn week'. The rows come from V03 §4.6's `plan` `WhySectionProvider` (l. 2377–2387: 'read from `PlanDamage` at the own level'), and `planDamage(doc, b, plan, view: ViewState, opts)` needs a view. But V10 §2.13 types the section provider as `rows(model: ModelView, id: Id, key: Knowledge)` (l. 990), with no view and no week. R4-05 gave the view only to the kind's `WhyProvider.explain` (`opts.view`), and neither §11.2's `why` comment (l. 16288–16290) nor V10 §3.9's query (l. 1642–1645, 'then appends the rows of every registered `WhySectionProvider`') passes anything to the sections. So an input that V03, V09 and V10 name has no producer. At a scrubbed week — a normal timeline path (V06 §3.15.2) — the plan panel shows that week's damage. One builder of the provider reads the document's current week; another cannot build the call. The card's 'Inside' section and the clerk's damage answer then differ from the panel beside them. T-V9-86 and T-V10-53 run at the head only.
required_change: (1) §11.2's `why` member (l. 16288–16290), after '… a provider that states no view's look ignores it': add '; a section provider whose rows are read at the drawn week — V03 §4.6's `plan` damage rows (V03 §5.6 (2) (d)) — reads that view's `week`, and with no view the document's current week (§2.9's `week` default)'. (2) END at V10 §2.13 (l. 989–990): `rows(model: ModelView, id: Id, key: Knowledge): WhySection['rows']` → `rows(model: ModelView, id: Id, key: Knowledge, opts: { view?: WhyProvider's opts.view /* the same view the kind's provider is passed (§11.2's view-bound why); a section whose rows read the drawn week — V03 §4.6's plan damage rows — reads view.week, else the document's current week */ }): WhySection['rows']`. (3) END at V10 §3.9's query paragraph (l. 1644): 'then appends the rows of every registered `WhySectionProvider` whose `appliesTo` holds' adds '— each passed the same `opts.view` —'. (4) END at V10 §3.23 row 14: the no-view outcome adds 'the `plan` section's damage rows at the document's current week'. (5) END at V03 §4.6's `plan` damage rows (l. 2377–2378): 'read from `PlanDamage` at the own level (V03 §5.6 (2) (d))' adds 'at the why's view's drawn week (`opts.view.week`, V10 §2.13; §11.2's view-bound `why`), else the document's current week'. (6) END at V09: T-V9-86 adds 'at a scrubbed week (V06 §3.15.2) the why card's `plan` section shows that week's own-level lines and head years, as the plan panel does'.

claim: A picture export draws a map's pins by default in one unit and never by default in the other. V09 §5.10's Picture tab (l. 4037) offers 'pins and public notes on · off (off by default)'. V09's entity table (l. 4137) says pins are 'never in pictures unless "Show pins" is on in the Picture tab'. §11.2's `ExportOpts` claims to declare 'every option an export reads … written by V09 §5.10's dialog' (l. 16197–16198) but has no member for that option. Its `furniture` is 'the picture's furniture (§9.5): default true' (l. 16219). §9.5's furniture list includes the Annotation layer ('numbered markers and a separate legend sheet', l. 15067). The measure tool's result 'can be saved as an annotation', which V09 §4.19 writes as a view pin ('Save as annotation writes a view pin labelled with the measure'). So an exporter built from §11.2 draws the view pins in every default picture. V09 offers the opposite default, and its switch has no member to carry it. This is two units with two outcomes for one case (a picture of a map holding pins), the class R3-03 grades major; the missing member is also VRC2T-12's class.
required_change: (1) §11.2's `ExportOpts`, after `furniture?`, adds `pins?: boolean;   // a picture (PNG, SVG, print): §9.5's annotation layer — the view pins and public notes (§2.9; V09 §4.19), drawn as the view draws them — over the map with the furniture; default false (V09 §5.10's "pins and public notes": never in a picture unless asked)`. `furniture?`'s comment reads 'the picture's furniture (§9.5), the annotation layer excepted (`pins`): default true'. (2) §9.5's *Annotation layer* bullet adds '(the view pins, §2.9; V09 §4.19 — in a picture only with `ExportOpts.pins`, §11.2)'. (3) END at V09: l. 4137's 'never in pictures unless "Show pins" is on in the Picture tab' → 'never in pictures unless the Picture tab's **pins and public notes** is on (§11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`)'; §5.10's Picture options cell 'pins and public notes on · off (off by default)' adds '(`ExportOpts.pins`)'. (4) T-ER-19 adds 'a picture of a map holding view pins with `pins` absent and true: no annotation drawn, then every pin drawn'.

claim: This round §6.1 *The weather stream* (l. 9561–9564) makes a press while a spell is in force wait until that spell's strength falls 'to 0 at its kind's fade rate (§8.4 (i))'; only then does the pressed spell start. §8.4 (i) (l. 13829–13830), the fades' home, states only 'at least 5 s for a shower, 60 s for fog, mist, dust haze and cloud cover, V11's rows never shorter'. It gives nothing for `snow`, `leaves` or `shimmer`, and only a lower bound for the rest. V11's rows hold no fade field (`ClimateSettings.weather.kinds` carries `lengthS` and `hours` only). So a press during a snow spell has no defined wait, though snow falls 3 an hour through a temperate winter. When the pressed spell starts is then undefined, and so is T124-9's replay of that case. §8.4 (i)'s own phase, V11 §3.25.11's rule (every `lengthS` lower end 'at least twice its kind's fade in §8.4 (i)') and T-V11-48 (c) also read a fade for every kind. Two builders would give snow different fades and start the pressed spell at different times.
required_change: §8.4 (i): 'its strength s in [0, 1] by its phase (rising from 0 and back to 0 over its fades: at least 5 s for a shower, 60 s for fog, mist, dust haze and cloud cover, V11's rows never shorter)' → 'its strength s in [0, 1] by its phase (rising from 0 and back to 0, each over its kind's fade: 5 s for a shower (`rain`, `drizzle`), `snow` and `leaves`, 60 s for fog, mist, dust haze, cloud cover and heat shimmer — each kind's `lengthS` lower end in V11 §3.25.11 at least twice it; §6.1's press reads the same fade)'. Every V11 row and override already meets twice these fades: rain 30, drizzle 60, snow 60, leaves 20, mist 120, cloudShadow 120, shimmer 120, dust 120, fog 180 s; arid rain 20–60 s.

claim: §8.8 (l. 14330–14332) applies a device-pixel-ratio change 'at once when no gesture runs, at the gesture's settle otherwise (T121-7)', with no rate limit, while the same unit's judgment J-A121.07 holds it to the loop's window — the base index row (l. 22865: 'a change Auto's loop decides while no gesture runs, and a device-pixel-ratio change, applied at once (at most once in 10 s)') and its Part A entry ('are applied at once, still at most once in 10 s') — and R4-10's binding phrase for 'Auto's or a device-pixel-ratio change's timing' ends '— and at most once in 10 s (§8.8)'. The repair's sweep wrote R4-10's phrase into §8.8's DPR sentence without its last clause. A window dragged to another monitor within 10 s of a loop change (an idle view stepped down under a weather spell, then moved): one builder applies the new DPR at once, another holds it until 10 s have passed since the last change. No bar separates them (T121-7 bars the re-evaluation only; T-ER-26's idle fixture has no change before it).
required_change: §8.8's sentence reads 'A device-pixel-ratio change (the window moved to another monitor) refits d at once and is applied while the view is settled — at once when no gesture runs, at the gesture's settle otherwise — and at most once in 10 s, counted with the loop's changes, so one coming within 10 s of the last change applies when those 10 s end (T121-7)'; T-ER-26 adds the input 'a monitor change with the view idle within 10 s of a loop step-down' with the outcome 'applied within one frame of the end of the 10 s since that step-down'.

required_change: §11.1's GeoJSON row adds, after the supplyChain clause: 'with ExportOpts.links (§11.2), one LineString of kind supplyLink per supply link within the export's scope — good, consumer, provider, satisfaction, declared, as the links query reads them (§11.2), a withheld end by address and kind and a concealed use's links left out'; §11.2's links comment cites '§11.1' for the feature (V09 §5.10 for the checkbox); V09 §5.15's row (l. 4126) reads 'one LineString per link within the export's scope (§11.1; §11.2's ExportOpts.links)' (V09's end).

claim: §11.2's out-of-range rule clamps 'vtt.squareM to the nearer of 1.5 and 1': a scripted 1.25 is equidistant, so two builders write a 1 m or a 1.5 m grid. A non-finite numeric member (NaN for vtt.pxPerSquare, stride or a size side, which a script or a bridged message can carry) is neither 'below 50' nor in the refusal list, so whether it clamps or refuses is unstated. Off the dialog's path (V09 §5.10 offers none), hence minor.
required_change: The rule reads '… vtt.squareM to the nearer of 1.5 and 1 (1.25 to 1.5, the default) …' and adds to the refusal list 'a numeric member that is not a finite number'; T-ER-19's out-of-range list adds vtt.squareM 1.25 and a NaN vtt.pxPerSquare with those outcomes.

claim: §11.2 now computes the listing at a drawn week from the frame ('read from V06 §3.15.2's frame (its Use records …; the HistoryStore images between the frame and the head)'), yet its closing sentence and §12.5's Find budget say the readers read 'the generation worker's Find index, rebuilt once per commit' (R12-35: 'the index once per commit'), while V09 §4.21.10 (7) rebuilds it also 'at each change of §2.9's week (a timeline scrub, a host's view.set { week }) and at each onEffectiveKey'. The base's trigger list omits the week and key changes its own rule needs, and no budget or timing bar covers the re-evaluation a scrub causes (T120-6 and R12-35 time a key's suggestions and a click's glow only; V06 §6.4 budgets the frame, not Find over it).
required_change: §11.2's sentence reads '… read it, from the generation worker's Find index, rebuilt once per commit and at each change of the effective key (§12.5), and, at a drawn week whose frame is not the head, re-derived from that frame at each change of §2.9's week (V09 §4.21.10 (7))'; §12.5's Find paragraph adds 'a change of the drawn week re-evaluates the chips' listing (§11.2's At a drawn week) off the scrub's path, within ≈ 100 ms of the frame being drawn at the METROPOLIS cap (V06 §6.4), the frame never waiting for it'; R12-35's row and T120-6 add that timing.

claim: V09 §4.21.12 (5) (l. 3641–3651) frames the crisis card's **Show** — and (7) Find's **Go to** on a look — on "the box of the marks `live.crises` draws for that look (§8.2's look rows, keyed by its condition, a preview by its look kind …), asked of the provider in the generation worker at the look's row's `band` over the map's `bounds` and that ring whatever the view (§8.2's `LiveLayerProvider.marks`)"; V09 §1b (l. 377) reads "`live.crises`' marks by look (§8.2)". §8.2 states no such key: *The layer* (l. 13134–13142) gives the marks only "of semantics `crisis.<part>`", and no column of a crisis mark is said to carry its look (`MarkTable.entity`, l. 12351, is unstated for them). The parts are shared between looks (l. 13084–13096): `campCluster` by siege, blockade, refugeeCamp, quarantine and occupation; `barricade` by blockade, raiders and rebellion; `crisis.ash` footprints by siege and raiders. With several looks standing — T-V9-85's own dossier fixture holds a siege, a refugee wave and a plague — a builder of `live.crises` from §8.2 gives V09 no way to tell one look's camps from another's, so Show and Go to cannot frame one look as V09 states: an input the build needs with no producer. Round 4's repair asked rendering (HAND-OFFS) only to name the reader.
required_change: Rendering §8.2 *The layer*, after "… and, a `base` layer, joins the tile key (§8.8).": "Each mark carries its look: in `entity`, the interned handle (§2.1) of the `ConditionOverlay` whose look draws it — a preview's marks none, the preview drawn alone — so one look's marks are told apart; V09 §4.21.12 (5)'s **Show** and Find's **Go to** on a look read them so, asking the provider in the generation worker for one look's marks at its row's `band` over the map's `bounds` and §8.8's ring, whatever the view, and framing their box." T-ER-27 adds "with a siege and a refugee camp standing together, every `live.crises` mark carries its own look's overlay, and the box of one look's marks holds that look's parts alone". (V09's text stands; its §1b row then cites a stated producer.)
